characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings (Book / Legendarium)
characters.summary: Boromir is a valiant mortal warrior of Gondor, fighting with a broadsword, shield, and the Great Horn of Gondor. He relies heavily on physical prowess, martial training, and sheer determination in melee combat.

techniques: Sounding the Great Horn of Gondor to rally allies and dismay enemies

weaknesses: Vulnerable to ordinary ranged weaponry such as multiple orcs firing arrows
Susceptible to the corrupting influence of the One Ring
limitations: Mortal endurance and vulnerability to lethal injury

sources.supports: General background, weapons, and death defending Merry and Pippin.

feats.claim: Fought fiercely against multiple orcs at Parth Galen before being slain by arrows.
feats.citation: The Fellowship of the Ring, The Breaking of the Fellowship

notableResults.citation: The Fellowship of the Ring (Film adaptation / Book events at Parth Galen)
notableResults.note: Boromir was overwhelmed by multiple orcs and archers after defending Hobbit companions.

conditional.ability: Stun or demoralize enemies with loud acoustic blast
conditional.dependsOn: Holding the Great Horn of Gondor

unknowns: Exact count of orcs defeated prior to his final stand.

characters.summary: Carcharoth is the greatest of the wolf-hounds of Angband, bred by Morgoth. He fights with immense physical strength, crushing jaws, and supernatural ferocity, augmented later by the burning agony of a Silmaril.

techniques: Burning agony inflicted by the ingested Silmaril

weaknesses: Driven to madness and self-destruction by the holy light of the Silmaril within his belly
Vulnerable to specialized hounds like Huan
limitations: Mindless rage when driven by pain from the Silmaril

sources.supports: Origins as wolf of Angband, swallowing the Silmaril, and death against Huan.

feats.claim: Bit off Beren's hand containing the Silmaril at the gates of Angband.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of Beren and Lúthien

feats.claim: Broke through the defenses of Doriath and rampaged through Beleriand.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Ruin of Doriath

notableResults.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Ruin of Doriath
notableResults.note: Fought the hound Huan to the death, resulting in the demise of both beasts.

conditional.ability: Burning touch that sears anything it contacts

campaignTags.claim: Described as the greatest and most terrifying wolf of Morgoth's breed, towering over ordinary wolves.

unknowns: Exact dimensions of the beast beyond being monstrously huge.

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings (Book / Legendarium)
characters.summary: Celeborn is an Elven lord of Lothlórien, fighting with a bow and Elven blade alongside Galadriel. He combines deep tactical experience with ancient Elven combat arts.
weaknesses: Vulnerable to fatal physical injury like any Elf
limitations: Bound to physical form in Middle-earth

sources.supports: Role as Lord of Lothlórien, husband of Galadriel, military commander.

feats.claim: Led the forces of Lothlórien across the Anduin to assault and raze Dol Guldur at the end of the War of the Ring.
feats.citation: The Lord of the Rings, Appendix B

notableResults.citation: The Lord of the Rings, Appendix B
notableResults.note: Successfully captured and destroyed the fortress of Dol Guldur.

unknowns: Extent of direct magical projection in combat compared to Galadriel.

characters.continuity: The Silmarillion / The History of Middle-earth
characters.summary: Celebrimbor is the greatest smith of the Second Age in Eregion, forger of the Rings of Power. In combat, he relies on standard Noldorin weaponry and defensive structures, though his primary mastery lies in craftsmanship rather than field generalship.
weaknesses: Deceived by Sauron regarding the craft of rings
limitations: Physical vulnerability in direct combat against superior numbers

sources.supports: Lineage as descendant of Fëanor, forger of the Rings of Power, death by Sauron.

feats.claim: Defended the gates of the House of the Mírdain against Sauron's invading forces.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Rings of Power and the Third Age

notableResults.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Rings of Power and the Third Age
notableResults.note: Captured during the sack of Eregion after a desperate defense.

conditional.dependsOn: Access to his forge and created artifacts

campaignTags.claim: Master craftsman who forged the Rings of Power and many technological/magical wonders of Eregion.

unknowns: Exact combat prowess compared to his grandfather Fëanor.

characters.summary: Celegorm the Fair is a son of Fëanor, known as a master hunter accompanied by great hounds, chief among them Huan. He fights with bow and spear, utilizing tracking and beast-mastery.
weaknesses: Ruthless ambition and betrayal leading to isolation and betrayal by his own allies

sources.supports: Son of Fëanor, alliance with Huan, conflicts in Doriath.

feats.claim: Captured Lúthien with the aid of Huan during the period of exile and betrayal.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of Beren and Lúthien

notableResults.citation: The Silmarillion, Of Beren and Lúthien
notableResults.note: Huan abandoned Celegorm and aided Lúthien, neutralizing Celegorm's advantage.

conditional.ability: Assistance from hound companion in combat

unknowns: Specific martial victories in major battles.

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings / The Silmarillion
characters.summary: Círdan is one of the oldest and wisest Elves remaining in Middle-earth, lord of the Havens of Mithlond. While primarily a master shipwright and counselor, he possesses deep wisdom and foresight.

mechanisms: Aegis of ancient wisdom and foresight

weaknesses: Aged and weary of Middle-earth wars
limitations: Reluctance to engage in aggressive warfare

sources.supports: Role as shipwright of the Grey Havens, bearer of Narya initially, extreme longevity.

feats.claim: Fought in the Last Alliance of Elves and Men against Sauron's forces.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Rings of Power and the Third Age

notableResults.note: Maintained the Havens and contributed forces to key defensive campaigns.

conditional.ability: Inspiring hope and endurance in others
conditional.dependsOn: Previously wielding Narya (the Ring of Fire) before gifting it to Gandalf

campaignTags.claim: Master of ships and havens, builder of maritime vessels for the Eldar.
Master of maritime craft and coastal havens.

unknowns: Exact combat engagements during the First Age.

characters.continuity: The Hobbit / The Lord of the Rings
characters.summary: Dáin II Ironfoot is a formidable Dwarf king of the Iron Hills and later Erebor. He fights with a heavy two-handed war mattock (ax-hammer), thick dwarven mail, and extraordinary physical resilience.

mechanisms: Exceptional dwarf stamina and stubborn endurance

weaknesses: Slow movement speed compared to mounted or nimble foes due to heavy armor and dwarven stature
mobility: Dwarven marching and running on foot
limitations: Limited mobility over long distances on foot

sources.supports: Role in Battle of Five Armies, King under the Mountain, death at Dale.

feats.claim: Slew Azog the Defiler outside the East-gate of Moria during the War of the Dwarves and Orcs.
Fought valiantly at the Battle of Five Armies at a great age.

notableResults.note: Beheaded Azog in single combat during the Battle of Azanulbizar.

notableResults.citation: The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A
notableResults.note: Slain defending the gates of Dale during the final days of the War of the Ring.

unknowns: Exact age at death in years.

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings (Book / Legendarium)
characters.summary: Denethor II is the Steward of Gondor, a proud and perceptive ruler. In battle and governance, he wields a longsword and commands the defenses of Minas Tirith, though his primary weapon in later years is psychological resolve and the palantír.
weaknesses: Deep despair and psychological manipulation by Sauron via the palantír

sources.supports: Role as Steward of Gondor, use of palantír, tragic death.

feats.claim: Maintained the defense of Minas Tirith against the armies of Mordor through strategic readiness.
feats.citation: The Return of the King, The Siege of Gondor

notableResults.citation: The Return of the King, The Pyre of Denethor
notableResults.note: Broken in spirit by Sauron's overwhelming will through the seeing-stone.

conditional.ability: Vision across vast distances and foresight

unknowns: Extent of direct battlefield combat feats in his youth.
